issues.title: Ending apartment vacation rentals and hotel rezoning of 48 properties

recap.headline: South Maui plan committee pauses meetings until virtual testimony returns
recap.in_60_seconds: The South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee met to review the policies and actions it has already adopted for the South Maui Community Plan. Before the review, members voted to finish this meeting but hold no further meetings until virtual public testimony is restored, after Planning staff said Akaka no longer has staff to run it; a separate motion to cancel this meeting failed. Four people testified in person: three residents and one representative of the Honuaʻula project, on emergency exits, a bike and pedestrian path along Pi’ilani Highway, a bypass road, project setbacks, cultural terms and native trees. The committee then adopted many policy and action changes without objection, including a path inside the 150-foot highway setback, a South Maui bypass right-of-way policy, protection of mature trees, more athletic fields and implementing wildfire plans. It is unresolved when virtual testimony will return, and whether the Council would extend the committee's deadline, now October 17.

parts.title: Opening and roll call
presented: Meeting opened at 5:30 p.m. with roll call and a Hawaiian-language welcome

parts.title: Agenda and debate over virtual public testimony
presented: Agenda: review adopted policies, sections 2.1 to 2.5, and adopted actions
Testimony accepted at the start or before each topic
A member moved to hold no more meetings after tonight until virtual public testimony is restored, citing growing written testimony asking for it
Members split: some said virtual access matters for people who cannot drive at night or have health issues; others worried about losing quorum and preferred working it out with Planning

answered.said: Virtual testimony depends on Akaka, which lost the two staff who ran it and is short-staffed; finding another provider would require procurement and take time.
The committee's extension runs to October 17; meetings at the Malcolm Center are booked through October 11; the Council could be asked for more time but may not grant it.

People can still testify in person or in writing, and the plan will have more public hearings before the Maui Planning Commission and Council; until the committee votes to transmit the plan, it can amend earlier decisions.
Planning can look at other options, such as a mostly virtual format like the Molokaʻi Planning Commission with a small in-person group, but the delay is not intentional.

next.what: No further committee meetings after tonight until virtual public testimony is restored
Planning to look for other ways to provide virtual testimony

parts.title: Motion to cancel tonight's meeting
presented: A member moved to stop tonight, saying decisions made without virtual testimony might have to be redone
The Chair noted members had prepared and people had already come to testify
Members confirmed testimony on topics not on the agenda can still be used later

parts.title: Public testimony on policies and actions
presented: Three people testified, followed by clarifying questions from members

raised.concern: Plan for emergency exits now, such as opening locked private roads or fire breaks during disasters, citing Lahaina
Build a separated pedestrian and bike path on the mauka side of Pi’ilani Highway; crossing at Līpoa Street is unsafe for students
Plan a tree-lined parkway bypass outside the growth boundary with no homes or businesses on it
Reference Kīhei road designs made about 20 years ago with a County grant in the plan
For the Honuaʻula project, the highway landscape setback may conflict with existing Phase II approvals and community agreements
The term wahi kūpuna raises legal concerns and may conflict with existing cultural protection laws; asked for a different term
Do not build a mauka-mākaʻi road in Honuaʻula; ranch and landowner roads already give emergency exits, and a road would harm rare native plants, wiliwili forest, bats and birds
Keep language that the County and State are not liable for shoreline loss, and hold those making recommendations accountable
Keep land in agriculture; farmers and their equipment helped contain the Kula fire

parts.title: Committee review of adopted policies, sections 2.1 and 2.2
presented: Committee adopted the final 2.1 policy, with a suggestion to define bypass and collector road in the plan
Committee adopted new 2.2 policies, including adequate parking for affordable multifamily housing
A member proposed a new policy encouraging public walkways when shoreline parcels are developed

answered.said: Under the Sunshine Law, public testimony must be taken again before each agenda item.

parts.title: Reopened testimony on policies
presented: One resident testified on section 2.5 cultural resources

raised.concern: Much of the cultural policy language overlaps the State Historic Preservation Division's Chapter 6E process, which already includes lineal and cultural descendants
Define wahi kūpuna, ʻike kūpuna, cultural practitioners and generational knowledge, possibly using case law, with place-based meanings
Find funding for a skilled team from the area to lead the cultural process

parts.title: Amendments to adopted policies
presented: Shoreline policy changed to designated, natural walkways rather than boardwalks
Policy 2.1.1 amended so the North-South Collector Road helps traffic travel through and out of Kīhei
Policies reinstated converting apartment-zoned vacation rentals to long-term housing; shoreline setback, fire-resistive shelter, drainage maintenance and require-not-encourage changes adopted
New policies: path within the 150-foot Pi’ilani Highway setback, shoreline buffers, early right-of-way for a South Maui bypass, and protection of mature trees

answered.said: A setback is normally measured from the edge of the highway right-of-way.
The original vacation rental language could help the Council make its case to phase out vacation rentals in apartment zoning.
Moved to add a pedestrian and bike path within the 150-foot highway setback where possible, based on that night's testimony; adopted without objection.
Moved a new policy encouraging early design and right-of-way purchase for a South Maui bypass, reflecting testimony; adopted.

parts.title: Review of actions
presented: Five Planning-suggested actions adopted: local resident preference for affordable housing, permanent deed restrictions, hotel green initiatives, visitor shuttles, and tax incentives for vacant commercial space
Actions adopted to buy a Kīhei parcel for open space and flood control and to make development and settlement-agreement tracking easy for the public
Action adopted to fund and find locations for more youth athletic fields across South Maui
Actions adopted to implement the 2016 South Maui Community Wildfire Protection Plan and the July 2021 wildfire prevention and cost recovery report

next.what: Members can propose more actions when the action review continues

parts.title: Late testimony on trees
presented: A resident testified on goal 2.5 trees

raised.concern: Prioritize native trees such as wiliwili and kou over invasive species like kiawe

parts.title: Closing
presented: Meeting adjourned

bills.name: South Maui Community Plan
bills.what: The long-range plan for South Maui whose policies and actions the committee is reviewing before sending it to the Maui Planning Commission.

bills.name: Honuaʻula Phase II approval
bills.what: Existing land use approval for the Honuaʻula project that its representative said the plan's setback might conflict with.

bills.name: Chapter 6E historic preservation review
bills.what: State historic preservation review process that a testifier said already covers much of the plan's cultural language.

bills.name: 2016 South Maui Community Wildfire Protection Plan
bills.what: Wildfire protection plan the committee added an action to implement.

bills.name: July 2021 report on wildfire prevention and cost recovery
bills.what: Report the committee added an action to review and implement.

votes.what: Finish this meeting but hold no further meetings until virtual public testimony is restored
Cancel the rest of this meeting
Adopt final 2.1 policy and new 2.2 policies
Amend Policy 2.1.1 on traffic through and out of Kīhei
Policy changes 2.3.8 to 2.3.14, including encouraging shoreline setbacks and fire-resistive shelters
Add maintenance to 2.3.10 and change encourage to require in 2.3.12
Add pedestrian and bike path within the 150-foot highway setback
New policy on early right-of-way for a South Maui bypass
Restore protection of mature trees in Policy 2.5.7

open_questions.question: When will virtual public testimony be restored so the committee can meet again?
Will the County Council extend the committee's October 17 deadline?
Did Corporation Counsel advise striking the language that the County and State are not liable for shoreline loss?
Is the term wahi kūpuna legally problematic in a community plan?

moments.who: a South Maui resident testifying on transportation
moments.quote: The fire breaks could be used as emergency exits because I don't want to burn up. I think it was pretty threatening and we know what happened in Lahaina.
moments.about: A resident asks that the South Maui plan include emergency exit routes, such as private roads or fire breaks, after the Lahaina fire.

moments.who: a representative of the Honuaʻula project's developer
moments.quote: Again, many of the members here are very familiar with the process that they've undergone, the lawsuits, the agreements that they've reached with the community in order to protect resources. They don't want something in the plan now that it's going to conflict with those agreements they've already reached.
moments.about: The developer's representative asks that plan language on highway setbacks and wahi kūpuna not conflict with the project's existing approvals and agreements.

moments.who: a resident whose family is from Honuaʻula
moments.quote: I appreciate that. Talking about over here inside, I see you guys. I don't think I'm at the level to talk about Honohumala, but it's important for me and my ʻohana that a road is not built, Mauka Tumakai, there.
moments.about: A Honuaʻula family member opposes a new mauka-mākaʻi road in the plan, citing existing ranch exits in emergencies and native plants and wildlife.
